summary: @onereach/idw-init-account-resources preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = `node setup.mjs`, which on `npm install` downloads the Bun runtime from oven-sh/bun GitHub releases, chmods the extracted binary executable, and uses it to execute the sibling file math_init.js — a 727KB bundled file whose top-of-file uses a string-array rotator (function WV8StW) plus a large numeric constant table to hide its control flow, URLs, and API surface. The loader setup.mjs is itself obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) and string-lookup wrapper objects. package.json declares `main: dist/index.js` but no dist/ directory is shipped in the tarball, so the package delivers no library surface; the only code that runs on install is the obfuscated Bun-executed payload. The advertised DB-migration/account-resource-initialization functionality is not wired to any exported entrypoint. Running an obfuscated payload under a freshly-downloaded alternate runtime at install time is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to bypass Node-scoped supply-chain scanning; the payload's behavior cannot be verified from source, and its purpose does not match the package's advertised function.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
